title: Sprint check-in: scrumban security sync & triage
body:
Meeting: Sec engineering sprint check-in (scrumban format)
Date: 2026-03-13
Time: 09:30-10:15 PT
Location: Zoom / #sec-triage
Attendees: Lina Chen (owner), Aaron Patel, Marta Ruiz, Evan Gold, Priya Nair, Tomás Oliveira, + ad-hoc from Platform (J. Kim), Observability (S. Rao)

Agenda:
- Quick wins and carryovers (5m)
- Vulnerability triage snapshot and decisions (25m)
- Secrets detection & rotation status (15m)
- Threat-model follow-ups: private deployments & cache exposure (15m)
- Action items, owners, and riskiest open questions (10m)

Summary / Highlights:
1) Vulnerability triage: We reviewed the prioritized list from automated scans and manual reports. Current critical/high items: SEC-4123 (privilege escalation vector in worker job manager), SEC-4180 (outdated dependency in embedding pipeline), and INFRA-789 (misconfigured S3 ACL in a staging bucket).
   - Decision: SEC-4123 requires a hotfix and immediate canary rollout on Dedicated clusters. We will patch the worker-job-manager container to disable legacy RPC endpoints and add a capability check. Aaron (owner) to produce rollback plan and test matrix by 2026-03-15.
   - For SEC-4180 we will schedule a dependency bump and extended integration tests; Marta to coordinate with Release Eng for a mid-sprint release.
   - INFRA-789: Platform to remediate ACL and run audit sweep across all staging buckets (not prod). Tomás to own and confirm via asset inventory scan (JIRA INFRA-789).

2) Secrets program update: The new secret-scanner (beta) flagged ~23 low/medium exposures across mono-repo; 3 were false positives, 4 are legacy test keys in archived repos, 16 require remediation.
   - Action: Priya to run targeted remediation sprints for the top 10 highest-risk leaks (based on key age and privilege). Prioritization rules: ephemeral vs long-lived keys, production scope, and service principal privileges.
   - KMS rotation: We have a partial rotation checklist for KMS-backed credentials; decision to pilot HSM-backed key for Dedicated customer with high-compliance requirement. Evan to draft HSM integration runbook and HSM test plan (due 2026-03-20).
   - Developer ergonomics: Scrumban note — reduce friction by adding a pre-commit hook that warns about candidate secrets; implement as opt-in, not blocking. Aaron to open PR with PoC.

3) Threat modeling follow-ups (private deployments & caching): The brown-bag tabletop last week surfaced a plausible lateral exfil via shared in-memory cache between tenant workloads in a misrouted private deployment.
   - Finding: If routing policy falls back to a wrong VM pool, KV cache entries could be exposed to a different tenant (edge case during autoscaling / migration).
   - Mitigations agreed: a) enforce per-tenant cache namespaces + token-bound cache keys, b) add a runtime assertion that rejects any cross-tenant cache bind attempts, c) extend chaos tests to simulate autoscaler churn and validate cache isolation.
   - Threat model owners: Marta to update the threat registry entry and add test cases; Priya to add observability signals (cache bind events and anomalous tenant ID mismatches).

4) Observability & alerting: We identified two noisy alerts that mask real signals: cache-bind-failures and ephemeral-token-renewal failures. Reduce noise by adjusting alert aggregation window to 10m and add a severity dimension for production vs staging. S. Rao from Observability will file the alert tuning PR.

Open questions / Risks:
- Does Dedicated still need a separate capability flag for the legacy RPC endpoints, or can we remove completely after the canary? Risk: brief compatibility break for older private deployments.
- Do we have budget/ops runway to pilot HSM in Q2 for one customer? Cost and procurement timelines unknown.
- Secrets scanner cadence: how frequently should we run repo-wide scans to balance noise vs surface area (weekly vs nightly)?

Action items (owner — due date):
- Aaron Patel: Hotfix & rollback plan for SEC-4123; canary test matrix (2026-03-15)
- Marta Ruiz: Coordinate dependency bump for embedding pipeline (SEC-4180); update threat registry and add test cases for cache isolation (2026-03-19)
- Tomás Oliveira: Remediate S3 ACL in staging and run inventory scan (INFRA-789) (2026-03-14)
- Priya Nair: Kickoff secrets remediation sprint for top 10 exposures; draft QA verification checklist for rotated keys (2026-03-18)
- Evan Gold: HSM integration runbook and test plan for Dedicated pilot (2026-03-20)
- S. Rao (Observability): Alert tuning PR for noisy cache/token alerts (2026-03-16)
- Lina Chen: Consolidate canary results and schedule post-mortem if rollback is used (2026-03-17)

Notes, context, and references:
- Refs: JIRA SEC-4123 (priv escalation), INFRA-789 (S3 ACL), Confluence Threat Model Registry (link above).
- Slack: #sec-triage pinned message contains short replay of triage decisions from Mar 10 thread.
- GitHub: PR templates and secret-scan action (repo: redwood/security-tools, PR #214 pending).

Misc / informal:
- We tried a short scrumban cadence for this meeting (3 focused items + 1 deep follow-up) — felt smoother than previous ad-hoc triage. Recommend we keep this structure for next 4 sprints.
- Note to self: run tabletop next month that includes a simulated partial rollback during autoscaler surge (to validate cache isolation and routing fallback).

Next meeting: 2026-03-20, 09:30 PT — agenda: post-canary review, HSM pilot go/no-go, secrets sprint kickoff.
